# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌 ☝ ✌ 👌 ✌ 🤟 👌 🤟]

The bomb shows display 0, a yellow light, and three wires in order red, yellow, blue. Mute has sent a nine-symbol gesture sequence; since Blind cannot see it, I will relay its symbols verbally so Blind can interpret it if the manual uses that code.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT yellow. WIRES: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's gesture sequence was: index pointing up, OK hand, index pointing up, victory hand, OK hand, victory hand, love-you hand, OK hand, love-you hand.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute’s symbols appear to use hand-number forms, likely grouping as `101 202 606` (☝=1, 👌=0, ✌=2, 🤟=6). I should give Blind that exact transcription, since Blind cannot see the gestures and may need it to identify the manual’s instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's nine gestures transcribe as digits: 1 0 1, 2 0 2, 6 0 6 — i.e. 101 202 606.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute has now sent the single gesture `✌`, which I interpret only as the symbol/digit 2, not yet as proof that wire 2 should be acted on. I should pass it to Blind exactly and ask Mute for an unambiguous encoded action instruction before Blind touches anything.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update: Mute has now sent one additional gesture: victory hand, which likely denotes digit 2. Do not act yet unless the manual independently makes the instruction unambiguous.")
speak(to="mute", text="I relayed your 101 202 606 sequence and your new 2 to Blind. Please gesture the final action unambiguously, ideally using a single gesture for the wire number if the manual says to cut one.")
```

WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute has repeated the same single `✌` gesture twice. Given the earlier encoded manual information, this is likely a deliberate final selection of number 2. I will report the repetition to Blind, while leaving the physical decision to Blind’s interpretation of the manual instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has repeated the victory-hand/digit-2 gesture again. Their last two messages were both 2; this likely confirms selection 2.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Blind correctly cut wire 2. The bomb has entered a new state: the light is now blue, wire 2 is cut, and wires 1 and 3 remain red and blue. Mute has again gestured `✌` (likely 2), so I will relay both the new visible state and the repeated signal to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Correct: wire 2 was cut. New visible state: DISPLAY 0; LIGHT blue; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact. Mute has again gestured digit 2.")
```

DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The new state was already broadcast to Mute and Blind last turn. No new manual signal or visible change has arrived this turn, so there is no basis to infer a further action safely.

``` 
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute has sent `🤟`, the same symbol previously used as digit 6 in the `101 202 606` sequence. I will relay this new signal exactly to Blind, without inferring a physical action from it alone.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's new gesture is the love-you hand, previously used as digit 6 in their 101 202 606 sequence. Current visible state remains: display 0, blue light; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact.")
```

Mute has now sent `🤟` followed by three `☝` symbols. Using the earlier apparent digit convention, that is `6` followed by `111`; I will relay it exactly to Blind for comparison with the manual.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest signals are: 6, then 1 1 1 (🤟 followed by ☝ ☝ ☝). Visible state unchanged: display 0, light blue, wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact.")
```

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Full post-wire-2-cut Mute gesture sequence in order: 🤟 ; ☝ ☝ ☝ ; 🖖 ; 🤟. The final 🤟 has just been repeated. Bomb view still: display 0, blue light, wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact.")
```
